lessons.title: Learn Flutter Lists in 4 Minutes | Create, Add, Remove, Loop - Step by Step
lessons.summary: Create a list, add Orange, remove Banana, and loop through it to build the screen — in 4 minutes.
lessons.body:
A List in Dart holds many items in one variable — here, a list of fruits.

1. Create — List<String> fruits = ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Mango'];
2. Add — fruits.add('Orange'); adds one item at the end.
3. Remove — fruits.remove('Banana'); takes that item out.
4. Loop — a for loop goes through every fruit and makes one ListTile for it, so the screen shows the whole list.

Because the list changes inside setState, Flutter rebuilds the screen and you see the new list right away. Download lists_example.dart, run it, press Add Orange and Remove Banana, and watch the total count change.

lessons.title: Dart List Methods in Flutter | map, where, firstWhere & sort
lessons.summary: Master essential Dart list methods like map, where, firstWhere, and sort to filter and transform data efficiently.
lessons.body:
Dart lists provide powerful built-in methods to transform, filter, and sort data with minimal code.

1. map — Transforms every item in a list into a new form and creates a new list.
2. where — Filters a list, keeping only the items that pass a true/false condition.
3. firstWhere — Finds the very first matching item, with an orElse fallback if no match is found.
4. sort — Reorders items in-place alphabetically or using custom criteria like string length.

Download main3.dart to run and experiment with these list methods in Flutter!

lessons.title: Set in Dart & Flutter | Unique Values, Union, Intersection & Difference
lessons.summary: Learn how Set in Dart automatically removes duplicate values and explore set operations like union, intersection, and difference.
lessons.body:
A Set in Dart is an unordered collection of unique items. Unlike a List, a Set will never contain duplicate values.

1. Automatic Duplicates Removal — Adding duplicate items into a Set does nothing.
2. Add & Remove — Work just like List methods using add() and remove().
3. contains() — Fast check to see if an item exists in the Set.
4. Set Operations — Perform union(), intersection(), and difference() between two sets effortlessly.

Download main4.dart to run and experiment with Dart Sets in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Map in Dart in 5 Minutes | Key-Value, JSON, Nested Data - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Master Map in Dart with key-value pairs, JSON parsing, adding/updating/removing entries, and nested data structures.
lessons.body:
A Map in Dart stores data as key-value pairs, similar to JSON objects.

1. Create & Access — Define Map<String, dynamic> and retrieve items by key using map['key'].
2. Add, Update & Remove — Modify entries effortlessly or remove unwanted keys with remove().
3. Keys, Values & Loop — Access .keys, .values, or iterate entries to build UI dynamically.
4. JSON Parsing — Decode JSON strings into Maps using jsonDecode() to handle API responses and nested data structures.

Download main5.dart to run and experiment with Dart Maps in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Functions in Dart in 7 Minutes | Define, Call, Parameters, Return - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Learn how to define, call, pass parameters, and return values with Dart functions to write clean, reusable Flutter code.
lessons.body:
Functions allow you to package reusable logic in Dart so you don't repeat the same code.

1. Define a Function — Specify the return type, function name, parameters, and function body.
2. Return Values — Use return to give back data (e.g. String greet(String name)).
3. void Functions — Use void when a function performs an action without returning a value (e.g. logWelcome()).
4. Parameters & Arguments — Pass variables into functions to make them dynamic and flexible.

Download main6.dart to run and experiment with Dart functions in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Parameters in Dart | Positional, Named, Required, Default - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Master positional, named, required, and default function parameters in Dart to build cleaner Flutter widgets and APIs.
lessons.body:
Dart parameters give you flexibility when passing arguments into functions and widgets.

1. Positional Parameters — Order matters: add(int a, int b).
2. Named Parameters — Wrapped in {}: createUser({required String name, required int age}). Order doesn't matter.
3. Default Values — Set fallback values: greet({String name = 'Guest'}).
4. Optional Positional Parameters — Wrapped in []: totalPrice(double price, [double discount = 0]).

Download main7.dart to run and experiment with parameters in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Return Values and Arrow Functions in Dart in 7 Minutes | Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Understand return types and arrow syntax (=>) in Dart to write concise, single-line functions in Flutter.
lessons.body:
Arrow functions in Dart provide a short syntax for single-expression functions.

1. Block Functions — Use curly braces and explicit return statements: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }.
2. Arrow Functions — Use => for single expressions: int add(int a, int b) => a + b;
3. When to use Arrow — Ideal for callbacks, list mappings, and simple getters.
4. When to use Block — Multi-step logic requires standard curly braces and explicit returns.

Download main8.dart to run and test block vs. arrow functions in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Null Safety in Dart in 6 Minutes | ?, ??, ??=, !, late - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Master sound null safety in Dart using nullable types (?), null-aware operators (??, ??=), assertion (!), and late variables.
lessons.body:
Dart sound null safety prevents runtime null errors by forcing variables to be explicitly nullable or non-nullable.

1. Nullable Type (?) — String? name = null; allows variable to hold null.
2. Null-Aware Fallback (??) — String name = userName ?? 'Guest'; provides a default value if null.
3. Null-Aware Assignment (??=) — city ??= 'Dhaka'; assigns value only if variable is currently null.
4. Late Initialization (late) — Declares non-nullable variables that are initialized later.

Download main9.dart to experiment with null safety operators in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Class and Object in Dart in 6 Minutes | Blueprint, Constructor, Methods - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Understand object-oriented programming in Dart by creating classes, instantiating objects, and defining properties and methods.
lessons.body:
Classes are blueprints for creating objects in Dart. Almost everything in Flutter is built using classes.

1. Class Blueprint — Defines fields (data) and methods (actions).
2. Constructor — Initializes class instances with data.
3. Object Creation — Create multiple instances with different data from the same blueprint class.
4. Methods — Perform actions on object data (e.g. user.greet()).

Download main10.dart to build custom classes and objects in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Anonymous Functions and Callbacks in Dart in 6 Minutes | Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Learn anonymous (lambda) functions and callbacks in Dart — the foundation of Flutter button onPressed handlers and event listeners.
lessons.body:
Anonymous functions (nameless functions) and callbacks allow you to pass executable code as arguments.

1. Anonymous Function — () { print('Tapped!'); } has no function name.
2. Callbacks in Widgets — Used in Flutter button handlers like onPressed: () {}.
3. Passing Functions as Arguments — Higher-order functions accept callbacks to handle events dynamically.

Download main11.dart to run and test callbacks in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Constructors in Dart in 6 Minutes | Default, Named, Factory, Const - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Master generative, named, factory, and const constructors in Dart to create efficient, immutable objects in Flutter.
lessons.body:
Constructors build instances of a class. Dart provides specialized constructor types for different needs.

1. Generative Constructor — Standard constructor initializing fields.
2. Named Constructor — Class.named() provides alternative ways to instantiate.
3. Const Constructor — Creates immutable compile-time constant objects for high Flutter performance.
4. Factory Constructor — Returns cached or custom instances instead of creating a new object every time.

Download Constructors.dart to experiment with constructors in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Encapsulation in Dart in 6 Minutes | Private, Getter, Setter - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Protect data using private fields (_) and control field access using getters and setters in Dart.
lessons.body:
Encapsulation hides internal class implementation details and validates data changes.

1. Private Fields (_) — Prefix variables with _ to restrict access outside the library file.
2. Getters (get) — Provide controlled read-only access to private data.
3. Setters (set) — Control and validate data before writing or updating fields.

Download ENCAPSULATION.dart to run and test encapsulation in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Inheritance in Dart in 6 Minutes | extends, super, override - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Reuse code efficiently using class inheritance with extends, super constructor calls, and @override methods in Dart.
lessons.body:
Inheritance allows a child class to inherit properties and methods from a parent class.

1. extends Keyword — Child class inherits from parent class: class Student extends Person.
2. super Keyword — Pass arguments up to parent constructor: super(name, age).
3. @override Annotation — Override parent methods to customize child behavior.

Download inheritance.dart to experiment with class inheritance in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Abstract Class in Dart | Blueprint You Cannot Make, Abstract Method - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Define abstract classes and methods in Dart to create shared architecture blueprints that child classes must implement.
lessons.body:
Abstract classes serve as blueprints that cannot be directly instantiated with new/constructor calls.

1. abstract Keyword — Prevents direct instantiation of the class.
2. Abstract Methods — Method signatures without a body that subclasses MUST implement.
3. Concrete Methods — Abstract classes can also include fully implemented helper methods.

Download abstract-class.dart to test abstract classes in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Interface in Dart in 6 Minutes | implements, Contract, No Code - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Use the implements keyword in Dart to enforce interface contracts where classes must fulfill all declared properties and methods.
lessons.body:
In Dart, every class implicitly defines an interface.

1. implements Keyword — Forces a class to implement all methods and fields of another class.
2. Multiple Interfaces — A class can implement multiple interfaces: class MobileApp implements Auth, Database.
3. Interface vs. Inheritance — Inheritance extends concrete code; interfaces enforce strict API contracts.

Download interface.dart to run and test interfaces in Flutter!

lessons.title: Learn Polymorphism in Dart in 8 Minutes | Real Shop App, One Call, Many Ways - Flutter Step by Step
lessons.summary: Master polymorphism in Dart to treat different objects uniformly through a common parent class or interface.
lessons.body:
Polymorphism ('many shapes') allows a single method call to execute different behaviors based on the runtime object type.

1. Uniform List — Store different child objects in a single parent type list: List<PaymentProcessor>.
2. One Call, Many Ways — Iterate through objects and call the same method; each class responds with its own implementation.
3. Real-World Usage — Essential for payment systems, custom UI widget lists, and clean architecture.

Download polymorphism.dart to run a complete Shop Payment example in Flutter!
